newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gen'l strike won't sway policy - Fernandez.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gen'l strike won't sway policy - Fernandez.

text.p: Economy Minister Roque Fernandez ruled out the 36-hour general strike by Argentine unions Thursday having any impact on the Peronist government's economic policy.
"No way are we thinking of changing the economic plan, because it is having remarkable success," he told reporters after the weekly cabinet meeting.
The general strike began today at noon local time/1100 EDT.

Fernandez's tax package, which was passed into law by Congress late Wednesday, is one of the austerity moves that has sparked the industrial action. The minister said the stoppage led by the main CGT labor federation "will not have a high level of success."

Underlining the determination of Peronist President Carlos Menem and Fernandez to stay on the path of free-market reform, Fernandez announced Thursday that the government would sell off shares in the state mortgage bank Banco Hipotecario.
The minister also said the government was considering an increase in public transport fares as a result of his hikes in fuel taxes.

Thursday and Friday's action was the second general strike in two months and was driven by discontent over 17.1 percent unemployment, by the new austerity package, and by Menem's drive for more flexible labor laws to favor employers.
